findings.title: Join timeout leaves flusher processes running
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join() sets the shared stopped flag, spends the entire timeout in next_step.join(), then breaks out of the process loop when remaining_time <= 0 before calling process.terminate(). Unlike the previous single-process join, a timed-out shutdown therefore does not signal or kill any flusher process that is blocked in Redis or Kafka future.result() and has not yet observed stopped. Those processes are not reaped on rebalance (the consumer process stays up; daemon exit only happens when the parent exits), so they keep flushing the same shards while the new assignment starts its own flushers. That races flush_segments/done_flush_segments and produces duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic.

findings.title: Restart starts a second flusher before the first is dead
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive() kill()s a hung SpawnProcess and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards without join() or any wait until exitcode is set. SIGKILL is asynchronous, and kill failures are swallowed, so the old process can still be inside flush_segments, produce, or done_flush_segments when the replacement process starts on the same shard list. Two flushers then mutate the same Redis segments and both emit Kafka payloads, duplicating spans. The replaced Process object is also dropped without join(), so each restart leaks a zombie until the consumer exits.

findings.title: Flusher metric tags embed comma-joined shard lists
findings.body: shard_tag is ",".join of every shard owned by the process, and it is sent as the statsd/metrics tag shard (and, on wait_produce, shards). With the CLI default of --flusher-processes 1, one process owns every assigned partition, so the tag value is a comma-separated list such as "0,1,2,...". DogStatsD encodes tags as comma-separated key:value pairs, so that value is parsed as extra tags and the timer is dropped or attributed wrong. It also makes the series cardinality depend on the partition assignment instead of a single shard id, and the same string is set as a Sentry SDK tag that will exceed the 200-character tag limit on large assignments.

findings.title: Flusher wait in test_basic is patched out
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to "give flusher threads time" after setting current_drift. That call hits the same patched sleep, so it does not yield. join() then sets stopped before the flusher thread is guaranteed to have observed the new drift and produced. The assertion (msg,) = messages can therefore fail intermittently, and the new test does not actually cover the multiprocess flush path it was adjusted for.
